assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks unite exquisite atomic control with an exceptional advance in time and frequency measurement.
assessment.attribution: Katori introduced the decisive lattice-clock concept and Ye made foundational experimental realizations and advances.
assessment.maturity: The clocks are deeply established, independently developed, and now enable tests and measurements far beyond laboratory demonstrations.
uncertainties: Credit for the wider clock-field infrastructure extends beyond two individuals.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their theoretical framework made trapped ions a compelling route to quantum computation and controllable many-body physics.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller supplied the central theoretical proposals connecting atomic control to gates and simulation.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have been extensively realized and have shaped a broad experimental field.
uncertainties: The relevant achievements connect to a larger quantum-information landscape with several potential prize framings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rydberg blockade turned strong atom-atom interactions into a remarkably versatile platform for programmable quantum matter.
assessment.attribution: These researchers made key theoretical and experimental contributions; the appropriate allocation of priority across the field needs close scrutiny.
assessment.maturity: Neutral-atom arrays have progressed from clean demonstrations to powerful, reproducible many-body experiments.
uncertainties: Mikhail D. Lukin is also an important contributor and the discovery-to-platform boundary is not sharp.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Titanium-sapphire technology and passive mode locking transformed ultrafast science and made attosecond physics possible.
assessment.attribution: Moulton's laser medium, Keller's mode-locking advances, and Sibbett's pioneering ultrafast work form a coherent account.
assessment.maturity: The impact has endured for decades across fundamental spectroscopy and precision control.
uncertainties: The technical and conceptual lineage includes many contributors, so a three-person attribution requires careful historical delimitation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry converted quantum coherence of matter waves into an extraordinarily sensitive precision-measurement method.
assessment.attribution: Bordé, Pritchard, and Kasevich represent major conceptual and experimental strands of the achievement.
assessment.maturity: The methods are mature, widely reproduced, and continue to yield stringent measurements of gravity and fundamental physics.
uncertainties: Priority and credit are distributed across several early atom-optics groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Preparation and measurement of mechanical motion near its quantum ground state confronts directly the quantum behavior of macroscopic objects.
assessment.attribution: Cleland, Aspelmeyer, and Kippenberg have each provided decisive experimental advances in quantum optomechanics.
assessment.maturity: Independent experiments have established quantum control, although the field remains rapidly developing.
uncertainties: The precise landmark that should define a prize, and the relative role of related electromechanical work, remain debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum control of ultracold molecules opens unusually rich tests of fundamental interactions and many-body quantum physics.
assessment.attribution: DeMille and Doyle are central figures in creating experimental molecular-control methods and applications.
assessment.maturity: The field has achieved substantial control and broad uptake, but its most distinctive fundamental results are still emerging.
uncertainties: Jun Ye is also central to major molecular-control advances; the field may be premature for a settled attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Direct laser cooling of molecules overcame a major obstacle to extending atomic quantum control to complex internal structures.
assessment.attribution: Tarbutt made a defining contribution to the experimental establishment of molecular laser cooling.
assessment.maturity: Multiple laboratories now cool and trap molecules, establishing the effect securely.
uncertainties: This achievement overlaps substantially with the broader ultracold-molecule program and may be better treated as part of a later, more comprehensive award.
